body.p: Set forth below in ascending order, with status identifiers, is a complete listing of all
body.h1: claims currently under examination. Changes to any amended claims are indicated by [[double
body.p: brackets]], strikethrough and /or underlining. This listing also reflects any cancellation and/or addition of claims.

br.br:
1. (Previously Presented) A device for use in sensing an analyte, comprising:a microneedle;
an electrode material on the microneedle;
a biorecognition layer on the electrode material, the biorecognition layer comprising a polymer, a biorecognition element configured to react with the analyte, and an interferent blocking agent that fills voids within the polymer, at least a portion of the interferent blocking agent being in contact with the electrode material; and
a diffusion-limiting layer on the biorecognition layer,
wherein the interferent blocking agent comprises polymerized phenol and the polymerized phenol is present within the biorecognition layer at a concentration of between about 0.1 mg/ml or 0.01% w/v and about 10 mg/ml or 1% w/v.
2. (Previously Presented) The device of claim 1, wherein the interferent blocking agent is non-conducting.
3. (Currently Amended) The device of claim 1, wherein the interferent blocking agent further comprises one or more of a polymerized form of resorcinol, hydroquinone, catechol, 9- phenanthrol, pyrogallol, [[and]]or a-napthhol.
4-5. (Canceled)
6. (Previously Presented) The device of claim 1, wherein the polymerized phenol is entrapped within the voids of the polymer.
7. (Original) The device of claim 1, wherein interference current at the electrode material of the device changes less than 70% over a one-week period.
8. (Original) The device of claim 1, wherein the biorecognition element is physically entrapped within the polymer.
9. (Currently Amended) The device of claim 1, wherein the polymer of the biorecognition layer comprises one or more of aniline, phenylene, phenylene vinylene, phenylene diamine, thiophene, 3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene, [[and]]or aminophenylboronic acid.
10. (Previously Presented) A device for use in sensing an analyte, comprising:a microneedle;
an electrode material on the microneedle;
a biorecognition layer on the electrode material, the biorecognition layer comprising a polymer, a biorecognition element configured to react with the analyte, and an interferent blocking agent that fills voids within the polymer, the voids traversing a thickness of the polymer; and
a diffusion-limiting layer on the biorecognition layer,
wherein the interferent blocking agent comprises polymerized phenol and the polymerized phenol is present within the biorecognition layer at a concentration of between about 0.1 mg/ml or 0.01% w/v and about 10 mg/ml or 1% w/v.
11. (Currently Amended) The device of claim 10, wherein the interferent blocking agent comprises one or more of a polymerized form of resorcinol, hydroquinone catechol, 9- phenanthrol, pyrogallol, [[and]]ora-napthhol.
12-13. (Canceled)
14. (Previously Presented) The device of claim 10, wherein the polymerized phenol is entrapped within the voids of the polymer.
15. (Original) The device of claim 10, wherein interference current at the electrode material of the device changes less than 10% over a one-week period.
16. (Original) The device of claim 10, wherein at least a portion of the voids are exposed to a surface of the electrode material.
17. (Original) The device of claim 10, wherein the interferent blocking agent fills at least about 80% of the voids within the polymer to limit access by interferents to the electrode material.
18. (Currently Amended) The device of claim 10, wherein the polymer of the biorecognition layer comprises one or more of aniline, phenylene, phenylene vinylene, phenylene diamine, thiophene, 3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene, [[and]]or aminophenylboronic acid.
19. (Currently Amended) The device of claim 10, wherein the diffusion-limiting layer comprises one or more of polydimethylsiloxane, polyurethane, polyvinyl chloride, polyvinylpyrrolidone, polycarbonate, polyethylene, polyethylene terephthalate, polyester, high density polyethylene, low density polyethylene, [[and]]or polytetrafluoroethylene.
